subject: Hosted API: fanout fallback caused degraded throughput — ClearHarbor
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearharbor.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API: fanout fallback caused degraded throughput — ClearHarbor

Hi Alicia,

Quick note to confirm we detected and are actively mitigating an issue affecting some requests from ClearHarbor to our hosted API. At ~07:50 PST we observed an internal routing change that triggered a partial fanout fallback to lower-throughput pools for a subset of requests to /v1/generate and embeddings endpoints. The visible effects on your traffic were:

- p95 for generate rose from ~210ms to ~1.2s for a ~40-minute window
- a small fraction (<0.8%) of requests experienced elevated retry rates
- no data loss; all payloads processed, some responses returned slower than expected

What we did so far:
- rolled out a soft rollback of a routing change within 15 minutes of detection
- temporarily disabled a fanout optimizer that surfaced a mismatched capacity profile
- collected debug traces and network dumps (attached: network-dumps.zip)

Immediate ask: if you have any request ids or traces you want prioritized, send them over and we will map them into our timeline.

Next updates: I will follow up within two hours with a mitigation status. Postmortem and timeline will be shared when we complete the internal review. We understand the impact to your SLA and will propose credits where appropriate once we finalize scope.

Apologies for the disruption — we know ClearHarbor depends on predictable latency.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the fast heads-up. We saw the elevated latencies on our end and it caused a backlog in one of our worker queues. Two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm whether model variant switching was involved (we saw a spike in model_load events)? If so, please roll back to the prior variant immediately.
2) We need an ETA for resolution and any temporary mitigations we should apply on our side (backoff, smaller batches).

We will pull logs for the request ids we saw and share any that might help. Also please flag if you plan to apply any credits — ClearHarbor will need that for our internal incident report.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearHarbor Logistics

Folks — forwarding ClearHarbor's reply. TL;DR: customer observed backpressure and wants confirmation + rollback. Current status: we disabled the fanout optimizer and are routing back to primary pools, but Alicia specifically called out model_load spikes which suggests a variant swap attempted at ~07:48 PST.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether the model variant swap completed for that pool (logs) and if we can hard-roll back to previous pinned variant?
- Marcus: re-check autoscaler events and capacity planning for the primary pool; if we need transient burst capacity we should enable it now to reduce pressure on their queue.
- Sean: suggest we prepare a short customer-facing note that confirms rollback and ETA, plus offer a token credit estimate.

Attaching our incident timeline draft for coordination (incident-timeline.pdf). I will handle the external message once we have confirmed rollback.

Thanks,
Hannah

Date: 2026-11-30T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API: mitigation complete — fanout fallback rollback and next steps

Hi Alicia,

Quick follow-up with the remediation summary and next steps.

What happened (summary):
- A routing experiment intended to reduce long-tail cost caused a fanout optimizer to select an under-provisioned serving pool for a subset of requests to your account. This produced model_load churn and higher p95 for a ~40-minute window on Nov 26.

What we did to mitigate:
- Nov 26 07:56 PST: disabled fanout optimizer for affected routing group
- Nov 26 08:05 PST: activated manual routing to primary pool while we monitored health
- Nov 30 15:10 PST: completed a controlled rollback of the routing state and removed the experiment configuration from production

Customer impact: elevated p95 and retry surface for a narrow window; no lost payloads; estimated 0.6% of requests from ClearHarbor experienced visible degradation.

Credits and follow-up:
- We will apply a service credit equivalent to one day of base usage for the impacted buckets; formal credit details and how to apply to your invoice will be sent by our billing team by Dec 2.

Postmortem and action items (available now):
- Root cause: missing capacity-matching rule in the fanout optimizer when the experiment targeted the serving group.
- Fixes deployed: capacity matching checks added, safe-guard canary, and an automated rollback trigger for variant mismatch.
- Next steps for you: no action required. If you want tighter controls we can pin model variants on your account or open a Dedicated capacity discussion.

Postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/clearharbor-postmortem-2026-11-30
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-26-fanout-fallback

If you want an internal walkthrough or a joint RCA session with your platform team, happy to schedule. Again — sorry for the disruption and thanks for working with us.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability Operations
Redwood Inference
